recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future build consumes the stale checked-in procedure.svg instead of regenerating from the StructureDefinition, address that as a build or diagram regeneration task rather than as an unresolved Procedure binding issue.
issue_request: FHIR-32815 was an Applied Patient Care change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking whether Procedure.performer.function should keep using Procedure Performer Role Codes when that value set mostly described occupations rather than procedure function. The accepted modification was to bind Procedure.performer.function to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/participant-role, with example binding strength.
initial_application: Commit 1c3625010a99e556dceb214ccadaedd0819dcdd8 applied the issue by adding the J#32815 committee note to Procedure.performer.function and changing the binding valueSet from http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/performer-role to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/participant-role. That commit also handled unrelated Procedure trackers FHIR-32513 and FHIR-41268.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Procedure as an active resource, and source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml now carries the J#32815 note and participant-role binding. The checked-in source/procedure/procedure.svg still has an older performer-role link, but it is a generated-looking diagram artifact and the current build.fhir.org Procedure page and SVG both render participant-role from the authoritative StructureDefinition. Zulip searches found no relevant discussion, and Confluence references only corroborated that FHIR-32815 appeared in Patient Care meeting minutes around the Jira vote.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative build-scope source and current generated publication surface already satisfy the Jira resolution, and changing only a stale SVG would be a diagram-only generated artifact edit rather than a semantic source fix.
